note: Majority: the Virgin Islands Code, title 16, § 261, as the Social Security Administration's legal opinion (POMS PR 07215.051) cites it: the age of majority is eighteen; the opinion adds that a minor of sixteen may be emancipated to administer property with parental consent and a court decree (16 V.I.C. §§ 231, 233) and that marriage emancipates (§ 221), neither held. The Code itself is published by the Legislature (legvi.org, behind a Cloudflare check that refused this client) and by LexisNexis, and wasn't read; the source is secondary. Work: the federal Fair Labor Standards Act reaches the Virgin Islands: 29 U.S.C. § 203(c) makes 'State' include any Territory or possession of the United States, and § 203(l) makes it oppressive child labor to employ anyone under sixteen (save a parent's own child outside manufacturing, mining and hazardous work; fourteen and fifteen may work in limited jobs and hours under the Secretary's rules, not held). Performers: § 213(c)(3): the child-labor provisions don't apply to a child employed as an actor or performer in motion pictures, theatre, radio or television, so free. The Virgin Islands' own child-labor law (in the Code's labor title) wasn't read, so any territorial work permit or stricter age isn't held; this should be checked. Service: none; there is no draft. 50 U.S.C. § 3802 makes every male citizen, and every other male resident, between eighteen and twenty-six register with the Selective Service System, a duty the form doesn't hold.

sources.title: Social Security Administration, POMS PR 07215.051 Virgin Islands (legal opinion)
sources.said: The age of majority is 18. V.I. Code Ann. tit. 16 § 261 (1995).

sources.title: GovInfo: 29 U.S.C. § 203, Definitions (Fair Labor Standards Act), United States Code 2023 edition
sources.said: "State" means any State of the United States or the District of Columbia or any Territory or possession of the United States. ... "Oppressive child labor" means a condition of employment under which (1) any employee under the age of sixteen years is employed by an employer

sources.title: GovInfo: 29 U.S.C. § 213, Exemptions (Fair Labor Standards Act), United States Code 2023 edition
sources.said: The provisions of section 212 of this title relating to child labor shall not apply to any child employed as an actor or performer in motion pictures or theatrical productions, or in radio or television productions.

sources.title: GovInfo: 50 U.S.C. § 3802, Registration (Military Selective Service Act), United States Code 2023 edition
sources.said: it shall be the duty of every male citizen of the United States, and every other male person residing in the United States, who, on the day or days fixed for the first or any subsequent registration, is between the ages of eighteen and twenty-six, to present himself for and submit to registration
